subject: Fit & replicability: recommended models, benchmarks, and emergency pin request
messages:
From: Karthik Iyer <karthik@redwood.com>
To: Aisha Khan <aisha@finpulse.com>, Tom Ruiz <tom.ruiz@finpulse.com>
Cc: Marissa Cole <marissa@redwood.com>
Date: 2026-09-21T15:12:00Z
Subject: Fit & replicability: recommended models, benchmarks, and next steps

Thanks again for the demo earlier — great discussion. Quick recap and suggested next steps for the evaluation we discussed (transaction classification + anomalous-activity detection):

Summary of recommended model variants
- Primary: Llama2-Chat-13B q4f16 (verified at 8k context for similar workloads) — best balance of latency and precision for your throughput profile.
- Fallback: Mistral-7B-Instruct fp16 — lower cost for less-critical routes.
- Pin candidate: Llama2-Chat-13B q4f16 @ v1.2.3 (we can pin on production to lock inference weights while you complete acceptance testing).

Assets I uploaded for your team:
- Benchmark CSV with precision/recall by prompt group. Link: https://drive.redwood.example.com/finpulse/benchmarks/FP-eval-pack-20260920.csv
- Prompt set (transaction samples + edge cases) included in finpulse_eval_pack_v1.zip (attached).
- Quick diff summary comparing our current prod model to the candidate in the attachments (diff_report_candidate_vs_prod_20260920.csv).

Immediate asks
1) Please run the primary prompt set and flag any failing examples (one-line note + sample prompt) so we can prioritize fixes.
2) Confirm whether pinning to v1.2.3 during your trial is acceptable — this lets us avoid noisy regressions from upstream model updates.
3) Let us know any regulatory/PII handling requirements we should reflect in the eval (redaction rules, retention limits).

Proposed timeline
- Today: you run the eval and return failing examples (target: 24–48 hours).
- 48–72 hours: Redwood delivers a focused model-variant plan and can pin candidate on your sandbox environment for verification.

If you prefer, we can schedule a 30-min triage session tomorrow to walk the failing prompts live.

Best,
Karthik
Enterprise Sales
Redwood Inference

-- Attachment: finpulse_eval_pack_v1.zip (zip, 6.2MB)
-- Attachment: diff_report_candidate_vs_prod_20260920.csv (csv, 42KB)

From: Aisha Khan <aisha@finpulse.com>
To: Karthik Iyer <karthik@redwood.com>
Cc: Tom Ruiz <tom.ruiz@finpulse.com>
Date: 2026-09-21T18:05:00Z
Subject: Re: Fit & replicability: recommended models, benchmarks, and next steps

Thanks Karthik — useful summary and thanks for the artifacts. Quick updates from our side after running the priority prompt set against prod: we observed a notable drop in precision on the ‘merchant-entity-normalization’ prompts compared to the demo results.

Example failing prompt (anonymized):
"""Normalize transaction description: "Pmt to ACME *INV 9923/NYC" -> expected: "Acme Corporation"; model returned: "Acme" (ambiguous)"""

Scope: ~1200 eval prompts run so far; precision down ~8 percentage points on that prompt group vs. the benchmark you shared. This is blocking acceptance for the classifier route.

Actions we need immediately:
- Evidence of where the candidate v1.2.3 differs from current prod (we saw the diff file but would like a short write-up of functional impact).
- If pinning is possible, we’d like Redwood to pin our sandbox to v1.2.3 and then to prod if the verification passes.
- If rollback is required, we may need an emergency rollback window while we validate.

Can we schedule the triage session tomorrow morning (US/Eastern) at 10:00? Tom and I will prepare a few failing examples and expected outputs.

Thanks,
Aisha Khan
Head of ML Ops
FinPulse

-- NOTE: We redacted customer PII in the sample prompts before sharing.

From: Marissa Cole <marissa@redwood.com>
To: Karthik Iyer <karthik@redwood.com>, Rishi Malhotra <rishi@redwood.com>
Cc: Aisha Khan <aisha@finpulse.com>, Tom Ruiz <tom.ruiz@finpulse.com>
Date: 2026-09-21T20:02:00Z
Subject: Re: Fit & replicability: recommended models, benchmarks, and next steps

Looping in the remediation plan — thanks for the signal, Aisha. Short plan from Product/Applied ML: 

What we’ll do (48-hour emergency lane)
1) Product will generate a targeted diff summary (top 25 prompts with behavior changes) and a small patch candidate (if applicable) or recommend pinning v1.2.3.
2) Ops will stage a pinned variant in your sandbox (pin = freeze inference weights + model id) for immediate acceptance testing. Pin staging target: within 24 hours.
3) If the pinned variant passes your acceptance tests, Ops will schedule a phased promotion to prod with canary traffic (5% -> 25% -> 100%) over 24 hours.
4) If the pinned/staged candidate fails, we’ll coordinate an emergency rollback to the prior stable model and run an ATA (acceptance test audit) to capture failing prompts.

Deliverables we’ll share:
- Top-25 diff report (CSV) + short prose summary of root causes (tokenization/context-handling regressions or decoding param deltas).
- Sandbox pin and a runbook that outlines rollback steps and expected RTO (target < 2 hours for rollback to stable).
- A/B metric dashboard link for your team to monitor precision/recall during canary.

I’ll take point on the diff summary; Karthik can lead the customer comms. Rishi — please confirm emergency pin authority and whether we should commit to the 2-hour rollback RTO for this tier.

Marissa
Director, Product
Redwood Inference

-- Attachment: planned_sandbox_pin_steps.md (text, 3.1KB)

From: Rishi Malhotra <rishi@redwood.com>
To: Marissa Cole <marissa@redwood.com>, Karthik Iyer <karthik@redwood.com>
Cc: Aisha Khan <aisha@finpulse.com>, Tom Ruiz <tom.ruiz@finpulse.com>
Date: 2026-09-22T09:40:00Z
Subject: Re: Fit & replicability: recommended models, benchmarks, and next steps

Approved: proceed with emergency pinning to v1.2.3 on sandbox and prepare rollback runbook. Ops — prioritize the sandbox pin this morning; coordinate with FinPulse for their acceptance window.

Notes and asks from leadership:
- Add the HubSpot deal id (FP-2026-0987) to the runbook and tag the incident for billing/credit review if we need to execute a rollback.
- CS should prepare a short acceptance-criteria doc (binary pass/fail per prompt group) so FinPulse can sign off quickly.
- Security: ensure the sandbox pin respects their PII redaction rules noted earlier.

Rishi
VP, Customer Success & Growth
Redwood Inference

-- Related: https://app.hubspot.com/deals/FP-2026-0987
